extracted.intended_audience: research administrators and institutional leaders at low- and middle-income country research institutions (CIDEIM and regional partners) preparing to manage NIH grants
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and implementing institutional policies, training, systems, and SOPs to strengthen capacity for administration of NIH grants at a LMIC research institution and for regional dissemination. Includes pre-award, award, and post-award practices, training curricula, and sustainability measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with NIH guidelines and requirements for administration of NIH grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall goal is to strengthen the capacity of CIDEIM to develop and implement institutional policies and practices for grants management that are compliant with NIH guidelines and requirements for administration of NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address critical gaps across pre-award, award and post-award phases; oversight of updated NIH guidelines; institutionalization through continuing education and updating training in accordance with changes in NIH guidelines; transfer capacity to other institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of senior administrators in US institutions (hands-on) and transfer of policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Train CIDEIM management leaders at Yale University (hands-on university training in grants administration) who will then transfer and implement these policies and practices including oversight of updated NIH guidelines in CIDEIM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes attending NIH regional events or NIAID post-award training and in-house training with the Grants Management Program (GMP) at NIAID to learn procedures to implement locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and adaptation of a Spanish-language training curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Design, implement and evaluate an internal training plan, curriculum and materials adapted to Spanish for research administrators and staff to fulfill NIH requirements for foreign institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial materials and trainer guide developed in Spanish, pilot-tested and adjusted; curriculum will be extended and updated according to institutional training needs and NIH policy changes; required sessions designated for specific audiences (e.g., all administrative/support staff must complete NIH fundamentals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to Sponsored Project Administration (SPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Introduction to Sponsored Project Administration (SPA)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will be required for all administrative and support staff as an entry-level session in the curriculum to ensure understanding of pre- and post-award administration responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort Reporting Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Effort Reporting Principles'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers principles for documenting and reporting personnel effort on sponsored projects; included in instructor-led modality at Yale and adapted for local staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading with influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Leading with Influence' to develop ability to enlist, persuade and engage others to obtain results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on workshop teaching influence approaches, power & relationship dynamics, and an influence model to set plans and enhance results; included to strengthen administrative leadership skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocating Allowable Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Allocating Allowable Costs'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach how to determine allowable vs unallowable costs under NIH policy and allocate budget lines appropriately for sponsored awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Compliance Principles for Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Research Compliance Principles for Administrators'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers ethical, regulatory, and compliance requirements administrators must observe (e.g., human subjects protections, COI, reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fly America and Open Skies Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Fly America and Open Skies Agreement'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers federal travel policy requirements relevant to sponsored projects and allowable travel procurement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Charging of F&A Costs on Sponsored Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Direct Charging of F&A Costs on Sponsored Awards'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers principles and restrictions for charging facilities & administrative (indirect) costs directly to awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Transfer Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Cost Transfer Principles'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach appropriate justification, timing, and approvals for cost transfers and institutional procedures to comply with sponsor rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Reporting and Closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'Financial Reporting and Closeout'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers preparation of financial reports, final financial reconciliation, invention statements, and final Federal Financial Report (FFR) for award closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: InsideOut Coaching (performance coaching skills)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training topic: 'InsideOut Coaching' — a one-day program offering a practical process for coaching to improve and sustain performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals include exploring ways to improve performance, applying a decision-making process, and using a coaching framework that compliments skills and moves people to action; included in curriculum for administrators and investigators seeking competency development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient Basics and Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Online training topic: 'Subrecipient Basics and Monitoring'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants will understand roles and responsibilities in the subaward process, differentiate subrecipients vs vendors, processes for subrecipient monitoring, invoice processing, and where to find institutional resources to assist with subaward monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing on Sponsored Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Online training topic: 'Cost Sharing on Sponsored Projects'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers definitions, documentation, allowable vs unallowable cost sharing, and institutional procedures for tracking and reporting cost share commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Research Staff Need to Know About Spending Sponsored Projects Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Online training topic: 'What Research Staff Need to Know About Spending Sponsored Projects Funds'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted information for research staff on allowable expenditures, documentation practices, and institutional financial controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle Investigator Eligibility: Who Can Be a PI?
rubrics_metrics.description: Online training topic: 'Principal Investigator Eligibility: Who Can Be a PI?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers sponsor and institutional eligibility rules for PI appointment and who may accept PI responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory audience-specific training assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH fundamentals session will be required for all administrative and support staff of the Promotion and Development of Research Capacity Unit (PDRC) and Administrative Unit; Introduction to SPA required for all administrative/support staff; other sessions required depending on job description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All investigators involved in NIH-funded projects, postdocs and project managers required to complete NIH fundamentals; audience varies by topic and job description; junior staff receive mentorship and technical competency development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot testing and iterative adaptation of training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial materials in Spanish for participants and a trainer guide will be developed and pilot versions will be tested as they are being developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot and adjust curriculum according to evaluation and training needs; extend and adjust training based on policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of Online components using ADDIE instructional design
rubrics_metrics.description: An online version of the NIH fundamentals course will be developed using the ADDIE instructional system design model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin development at end of year 1, evaluate feasibility to virtualize other courses after assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of an in-house Grant Tracking System
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a new in-house Grant Tracking System integrating previous administrative and training tracking applications to manage Pre-Award and Post-Award processes at CIDEIM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System to be used by all administrators, support staff and researchers involved in grants management; leverage prior applications (administrative tracking, training tracking, study progress dashboard); include web and mobile access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment and harmonization of institutional policies, procedures and SOPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional policies, procedures and SOPs will be revised to assure and harmonize compliance with Federal requirements, including Public Access Policy, Policy on Financial Conflicts of Interest, Procedure for Research Misconduct, Procedures for Human Subjects, Policy and Procedures on Monitoring of Performance by Consortium Institutions, Procedures describing the process required to change an established budget, Human Subjects Research Training SOP, Grants Administration/Financial Management SOPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and update in light of Yale and NIH policies learned during training; institutionalize 'how, who, when, what and why' for functions that currently lack detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reporting and closeout requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting obligations include annual RPPR and final RPPR, invention statement and final FFR for award closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop strategies for improving grants management oversight and business practices and produce reports stating changes initiated/made to local business practices and staff training plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award institutional registrations and administrative readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain institutional registrations required for application to funding agencies (such as DUNS, SAMS, eRA Commons and others) up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Promotion and Development Unit manages institutional registrations, assists investigators in identifying funding opportunities, ensures compliance with agency instructions, and manages internal review for institutional approval to submit applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management systems and external audit practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial management through accounting software (UNO-EE), payroll/health software (UNO85C), adoption of IFRS, bank arrangements for international transactions, and continuous external auditing (monthly monitoring visits and comprehensive audits every trimester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial Manager coordinates internal and external reporting, tax returns, interacts with external auditors for monitoring and assistance; systems must enable tracking grant expenditures and development of financial status reports for projects and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Office disseminates institutional, national and international quality requirements; CIDEIM is GCP certified by INVIMA and has a Quality Management System responding to health research requirements (habilitation of services, management of human samples/biological collections, access to genetic resources, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate quality initiatives across units and ensure compliance with national standards for health research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical review and human subjects protection adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ethical Review Committee adheres to Colombian National Resolution 8430/93, National Resolution 2378/2008 (good clinical practices), Declaration of Helsinki (2013), CIOMS international ethical guidelines (2016), and U.S. Code of Federal Regulations Title 45 Part 46; CIDEIM holds Federal Wide Assurance (FWA) approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRB composition, external members, procedures for ethical review, monitoring of projects, reporting of adverse events, and assurance of participant confidentiality are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and biostatistics standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Biostatistics and Epidemiology Unit responsibilities include sample size calculations, sampling methods, statistical analysis, preparation of reports and publications, and data management practices such as development of databases, custom data entry screens, double data entry and interactive checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of software (STATA, R, SQLServer, Epi Info) and ensuring valid, traceable data and quantitative analysis for research studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core laboratory biosafety and contamination-avoidance practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities (PCR/qPCR facility, culture facilities, BSL-2/3 areas) must have designated and segregated areas for different steps (e.g., molecular amplification) to avoid carryover and contamination; appropriate biosafety features for high-risk organisms (negative-pressure rooms, biosafety hoods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish controlled-access areas, temperature-controlled equipment rooms, and facility-specific SOPs to meet biosafety requirements for work with pathogens and human samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biobank management and specimen storage standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Biobank must maintain well-characterized collections (e.g., strains and isolates) with appropriate storage equipment (liquid nitrogen storage vessels, -80°C ultrafreezers) and management systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve DNA/plasma samples, maintain catalogs and capacity information, and ensure management procedures for biological materials are in place and supervised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward management responsibilities and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand requirements for establishing and monitoring subawards, roles and responsibilities of PI and administrators throughout the subaward process, including differentiating a subrecipient from a vendor, subrecipient monitoring, and invoice processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training outcomes include understanding where to find institutional resources for subaward processing and compliance, and awareness of university policies/expectations for subrecipient monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language accessibility for sustainability (Spanish adaptation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because many administrative staff do not speak English, curriculum must be adapted and translated into Spanish to ensure effective implementation and regional applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make materials and online components accessible in Spanish and offer recorded webinars/post-seminar forums via the virtual campus so regional participants can access content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability initiatives: institutional oversight and clear procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainability initiatives include adjustment of institutional policies/SOPs to manage NIH grants, development of online components for training, and development of an in-house grants tracking system to promote sustainability of practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clarifying roles/responsibilities and documenting 'how, who, when, what and why' across functions to facilitate long-term grants administration improvements.
